translationRepairs: Earlier Gaozu had planned to change the reign title. The Secretariat and Chancellery proposed the two characters "Qianhe," but Gaozu changed it to Qianyou; it now coincided with his imperial name.

Earlier Gaozu had planned to change the reign title. The Secretariat and Chancellery proposed the two characters "Qianhe," but Gaozu changed it to Qianyou; at this point it matched the reigning emperor's personal name.
與御名相符 refers to the reigning Emperor Yin's personal name Chengyou, not Gaozu's.

On dingwei Li Shi, Director of the Imperial Household, became Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; Bian Guidang moved from Vice Minister of Rites to Vice Minister of Justice; and Lu Jia from Vice Minister of Justice to Vice Minister of War.

Liu Chong, Northern Capital garrison commander, Acting Grand Commandant, and Concurrent Councilor of the Second Rank, was also made military governor of Songzhou; and Shi Hongzhao, commander of the palace guard horse and foot and Concurrent Councilor of the Second Rank, was additionally promoted to Acting Grand Preceptor and Concurrent Palace Attendant;

Liu Chong, Northern Capital garrison commander, Acting Grand Commandant, and Concurrent Councilor of the Second Rank, and Shi Hongzhao, military governor of Songzhou, commander-in-chief of the palace guard cavalry and infantry, Acting Grand Commandant, and Concurrent Councilor of the Second Rank, were both additionally made Acting Grand Preceptor and Concurrent Palace Attendant;
The final 並加 applies to both men, while the Songzhou governorship and palace-guard command are Shi Hongzhao's offices.
Liu Xin, military governor of Xuzhou, deputy commander of the palace guard, Acting Grand Commandant, and Concurrent Councilor of the Second Rank, was promoted to Acting Grand Preceptor.
Liu Xin, military governor of Xu Prefecture, deputy commander of the palace guard, Acting Grand Commandant, and Concurrent Councilor of the Second Rank, was promoted to Acting Grand Preceptor.
許州 is Xu Prefecture, centered on Xuchang, not 徐州 (Xuzhou).
Liu Zhu of Qingzhou and Murong Yanchao of Yanzhou, each Acting Grand Commandant and Concurrent Councilor of the Second Rank, were both promoted to Acting Grand Preceptor.
Liu Zhu of Qingzhou and Murong Yanchao of Yunzhou, each Acting Grand Commandant and Concurrent Councilor of the Second Rank, were both promoted to Acting Grand Preceptor.
鄆州 is Yunzhou, not 兗州 (Yanzhou).
Guo Congyi of Caozhou and Xue Huairang of Xingzhou were each promoted from Acting Grand Tutor to Acting Grand Commandant;
Guo Congyi of Chanzhou and Xue Huairang of Xingzhou were each promoted from Acting Grand Tutor to Acting Grand Commandant;
澶州 is Chanzhou; Caozhou is a different prefecture.

Fu Yanqing, military governor of Yanzhou, Acting Grand Preceptor, Concurrent Palace Attendant, and Duke of Qi of Fengxiang, was also made Concurrent Chief Councilor and enfeoffed as Duke of Wei;
The parenthetical graph distinguishes the homophonous fief 岐 from 齊 later in the same list.

Guo Jin, military governor of Hua Prefecture and Acting Grand Commandant, was made military governor of Binzhou;

That same day Guo Congyi, military governor of Chanzhou, was appointed overall commander of the Yongxing Army's horse and foot forces.
澶州 is Chanzhou; Caozhou is a different prefecture.

澶州 is Chan Prefecture; Cao Prefecture is a different place.
